title: Powering the agents: Workers AI now runs large models, starting with Kimi K2.5
partialText: Kimi K2.5 is now on Workers AI, helping you power agents entirely on Cloudflare’s Developer Platform. Learn how we optimized our inference stack and reduced inference costs for internal agent use cases.

title: Introducing Custom Regions for precision data control
partialText: We are expanding Regional Services with new pre-defined regions and the launch of Custom Regions. Customers can now define precise geographical boundaries for data processing, tailored to meet their compliance and performance needs.

title: Standing up for the open Internet: why we appealed Italy’s "Piracy Shield" fine
partialText: Cloudflare is appealing a €14 million fine from Italian regulators over "Piracy Shield," a system that forces providers to block content without oversight. We are challenging this framework to protect the Internet from disproportionate overblocking and lack of due process.

title: From legacy architecture to Cloudflare One
partialText: Learn how Cloudflare and CDW de-risk SASE migrations with a blueprint that treats legacy debt as an application modernization project.

title: Announcing Cloudflare Account Abuse Protection: prevent fraudulent attacks from bots and humans
partialText: Blocking bots isn’t enough anymore. Cloudflare’s new fraud prevention capabilities — now available in Early Access — help stop account abuse before it starts.

title: Slashing agent token costs by 98% with RFC 9457-compliant error responses
partialText: Cloudflare now returns RFC 9457-compliant structured Markdown and JSON error payloads to AI agents, replacing heavyweight HTML pages with machine-readable instructions. This reduces token usage by over 98%, turning brittle parsing into efficient control flow.

title: AI Security for Apps is now generally available
partialText: Cloudflare AI Security for Apps is now generally available, providing a security layer to discover and protect AI-powered applications, regardless of the model or hosting provider. We are also making AI discovery free for all plans, to help teams find and secure shadow AI deployments.

title: Investigating multi-vector attacks in Log Explorer
partialText: Log Explorer customers can now identify and investigate multi-vector attacks. Log Explorer supports 14 additional Cloudflare datasets, enabling users to have a 360-degree view of their network.

title: Building a security overview dashboard for actionable insights
partialText: Cloudflare's new Security Overview dashboard transforms overwhelming security data into prioritized, actionable insights, empowering defenders with contextual intelligence on vulnerabilities.

title: Translating risk insights into actionable protection: leveling up security posture with Cloudflare and Mastercard
partialText: Cloudflare will be integrating Mastercard’s RiskRecon attack surface intelligence capabilities to help you eliminate Internet-facing blind spots while continuously monitoring and closing security gaps.

title: Fixing request smuggling vulnerabilities in Pingora OSS deployments
partialText: Today we’re disclosing request smuggling vulnerabilities when our open source Pingora service is deployed as an ingress proxy and how we’ve fixed them in Pingora 0.8.0.

title: Active defense: introducing a stateful vulnerability scanner for APIs
partialText: Cloudflare’s new Web and API Vulnerability Scanner helps teams proactively find logic flaws. By using AI to build API call graphs, we identify vulnerabilities that standard defensive tools miss.

title: Complexity is a choice. SASE migrations shouldn’t take years.
partialText: Discover how Cloudflare partners TachTech and Adapture are shattering the 18-month migration myth, deploying agile SASE for global enterprises in weeks by treating security as software.

title: From the endpoint to the prompt: a unified data security vision in Cloudflare One
partialText: Cloudflare One unifies data security from endpoint to prompt: RDP clipboard controls, operation-mapped logs, on-device DLP, and Microsoft 365 Copilot scanning via API CASB.

title: Ending the "silent drop": how Dynamic Path MTU Discovery makes the Cloudflare One Client more resilient
partialText: The Cloudflare One Client now features the ability to actively probe and adjust packet sizes. This update eliminates the problems caused by tunnel layering and MTU differences, providing more stability and resiliency.

title: How Automatic Return Routing solves IP overlap
partialText: Automatic Return Routing (ARR) solves the common enterprise challenge of overlapping private IP addresses by using stateful flow tracking instead of traditional routing tables. This userspace-driven approach ensures return traffic reaches the correct origin tunnel without manual NAT or VRF configuration.

title: A QUICker SASE client: re-building Proxy Mode
partialText: By transitioning the Cloudflare One Client to use QUIC streams for Proxy Mode, we eliminated the overhead of user-space TCP stacks, resulting in a 2x increase in throughput and significant latency reduction for end users.

title: Always-on detections: eliminating the WAF “log versus block” trade-off
partialText: Cloudflare is introducing Attack Signature Detection and Full-Transaction Detection to provide continuous, high-fidelity security insights without the manual tuning of traditional WAFs. By correlating request payloads with server responses, we can now identify successful exploits and data exfiltration while minimizing false positives.

title: Mind the gap: new tools for continuous enforcement from boot to login
partialText: Cloudflare’s mandatory authentication and independent MFA protect organizations by ensuring continuous enforcement, from the moment a machine boots until sensitive resources are accessed.

title: Defeating the deepfake: stopping laptop farms and insider threats
partialText: Cloudflare One is partnering with Nametag to combat laptop farms and AI-enhanced identity fraud by requiring identity verification during employee onboarding and via continuous authentication.
